correctness.rationale: The line-graph identification converts dissociation into a packing of isolated edges and two-edge paths. The 2/3 vertex-capacity bound is sharp only for a spanning P3-factor. Bipartition equations force k row centers and k column centers. One replacement cannot change a saturated two-edge star. For two replacements, the complete local classification is leaf exchanges within two stars of one orientation (8 binom(k,2)) or paired recentering across opposite orientations (4k^2). Center-set fibers are connected via leaf transpositions and the quotient realizes the connected tensor product of two nonbipartite Johnson graphs. Two independent executable enumerations give 9 states/degree4 and 8100 states/degree24, with one component for n=3 and n=6; the proof, not computations, covers all k.

evidence: Bonsma, Kamiński and Wrochna (2014) Theorem 16 treats reachability among independent sets of claw-free graphs, including line graphs. The 2010/2011 Orlovich preprint proves a general computational hardness and P3-packing reduction for dissociation sets.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The independent-set theorem has the wrong feasible objects: each optimum dissociation set here induces 2k edges, hence is not independent. The general dissociation-set hardness result has no two-simultaneous-replacement connectivity theorem. Neither result dominates the stated claim.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the sharp one-versus-two simultaneous-replacement mobility threshold and the full regular degree for every 3k square rook graph. Orlovich et al. already give the line-graph P3 packing equivalence, and a prior rectangular-rook induced-matching enumeration implies the optimum count, so these are explicitly excluded from the originality claim. Bonsma et al. address independent set token moves in claw-free graphs; the present selected sets induce many adjacent pairs. Prior triangular-graph maximum-dissociation reconfiguration concerns line graphs of complete rather than complete bipartite graphs and does not imply this center-fiber mechanism. Targeted record and primary literature searches found no implication covering the mobility theorem; not a proof of publication uniqueness.
residual_risks: Equivalent two-swap connectivity results may be published under P3-factor, partial star factor, or exact-cover terminology but absent from indexed searches.

value.rationale: This is a motivated sharp budget transition in the entire optimum space of a familiar highly symmetric graph family: every optimum is frozen under one selected-square replacement but all are connected under two simultaneous replacements, with explicit regular degree and a constructive path to arbitrary center sets. The 3-vertex path-factor mechanism is structural, not a renaming or a known table count; the exact count is credited as known. It gives a precise repair threshold for locally frozen optimum placements and general k proof, unlike an arbitrary small invariant.
